title: Are people loyal to brands
paragraphs: You might have heard the term 'brand loyalty'. As we enter a 5th generation of console releases, with Sony's PS5 and Microsoft's Xbox series X due to hit our shelves this year, once more psychologists are predicting a wave of purchases based on fidelity.

But why do people feel compelled to stick with brands? Writer Carol M. Bopp describes brand loyalty as a positive feeling that consumers identify with a certain product or company. This also draws on the idea of brand awareness: the extent to which customers are familiar with the logo or values of a brand, goods or a service.

Huge companies pump millions into marketing and advertising, using analytics to determine who is their ICP, or ideal customer profile. It’s no surprise that the ads which pop up on social media somehow feel targeted at or tailored for you. This is because companies spend a lot of time and money analysing who is most likely to become loyal customers.

This extends to the supermarkets. Many believe that the more expensive branded products are much better than the supermarkets’ own brand. Money-saving experts like Martin Lewis, encourage us to give up the premium or branded products and buy the value versions.

So, are we really brand loyal? Companies certainly want us to be. But there are those who believe it's more to do with brand habit – that feeling of comfort you get from buying the same product over and over again. Once we’re familiar with a brand and we know that it's OK, we don't feel compelled to try anything else.

So, the next time you find yourself buying your favourite brand, it might not be down to brand loyalty, but rather to habit, or even that you have been targeted by a specific company through tailored ads.

vocabulary.entry: brand loyalty /brænd ˈlɔɪəlti/ n. 品牌忠诚度
vocabulary.example: Brand loyalty is crucial for the long-term success of a business.
vocabulary.translation: 品牌忠诚度对企业的长远发展至关重要。

vocabulary.entry: console release /kənˈsəʊl rɪˈliːs/ n. 游戏机发售
vocabulary.example: The console release was accompanied by a lot of promotional events.
vocabulary.translation: 这款游戏机发售时配套举办了很多促销活动。

vocabulary.entry: fidelity /fɪˈdeləti/ n. 忠诚度；忠实度
vocabulary.example: The brand has a strong base of customers with high fidelity.
vocabulary.translation: 该品牌拥有一群忠诚度极高的核心客户。

vocabulary.entry: feel compelled to /fiːl kəmˈpeld tuː/ 忍不住；感觉必须做
vocabulary.example: I feel compelled to help her when she's in trouble.
vocabulary.translation: 她遇到困难时，我忍不住想要帮她。

vocabulary.entry: stick with /stɪk wɪð/ 坚持；继续使用
vocabulary.example: He decided to stick with his original plan despite the difficulties.
vocabulary.translation: 尽管困难重重，他还是决定坚持自己最初的计划。

vocabulary.entry: identify with /aɪˈdentɪfaɪ wɪð/ 认同；产生共鸣
vocabulary.example: Many readers can identify with the main character in the novel.
vocabulary.translation: 很多读者都能与小说中的主角产生共鸣。

vocabulary.entry: brand awareness /brænd əˈweənəs/ n. 品牌认知度
vocabulary.example: The campaign is designed to increase brand awareness among young people.
vocabulary.translation: 这次宣传活动旨在提高年轻人对该品牌的认知度。

vocabulary.entry: logo /ˈləʊɡəʊ/ n. 标志；标识
vocabulary.example: The company changed its logo to reflect its new brand image.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司更换了标志，以体现全新的品牌形象。

vocabulary.entry: pump into /pʌmp ˈɪntuː/ 投入（资金、时间等）
vocabulary.example: The government plans to pump more money into education.
vocabulary.translation: 政府计划向教育领域投入更多资金。

vocabulary.entry: marketing /ˈmɑːkɪtɪŋ/ n. 市场营销
vocabulary.example: She works in the marketing department of a large company.
vocabulary.translation: 她在一家大公司的市场营销部门工作。

vocabulary.entry: advertising /ˈædvətaɪzɪŋ/ n. 广告宣传
vocabulary.example: The company's advertising has helped boost its sales significantly.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司的广告宣传极大地推动了产品销量。

vocabulary.entry: analytics /ˌænəˈlɪtɪks/ n. 数据分析
vocabulary.example: The team uses analytics to understand customer behaviour better.
vocabulary.translation: 该团队借助数据分析来更深入地了解客户行为。

vocabulary.entry: ideal customer profile /aɪˈdɪəl ˈkʌstəmə ˈprəʊfaɪl/ n. 理想客户画像
vocabulary.example: The company has defined its ideal customer profile based on market research.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司根据市场调研确定了理想客户画像。

vocabulary.entry: pop up /pɒp ʌp/ 突然出现；弹出
vocabulary.example: A window popped up asking me to update the software.
vocabulary.translation: 一个提示软件更新的窗口突然弹了出来。

vocabulary.entry: target at /ˈtɑːɡɪt æt/ 以……为目标
vocabulary.example: The new product is targeted at young professionals aged 25 to 35.
vocabulary.translation: 这款新产品的目标受众是25至35岁的年轻职场人士。

vocabulary.entry: tailor for /ˈteɪlə fɔː/ 为……量身定制
vocabulary.example: The course is tailored for students with no prior knowledge of the subject.
vocabulary.translation: 这门课程是为没有该学科基础的学生量身定制的。

vocabulary.entry: own brand /əʊn brænd/ n. 自有品牌
vocabulary.example: The supermarket's own brand products are cheaper and of good quality.
vocabulary.translation: 这家超市的自有品牌产品价格实惠且质量不错。

vocabulary.entry: money-saving expert /ˈmʌni ˈseɪvɪŋ ˈekspɜːt/ n. 省钱专家
vocabulary.example: The money-saving expert shared some tips for cutting household expenses.
vocabulary.translation: 这位省钱专家分享了一些削减家庭开支的小窍门。

vocabulary.entry: premium product /ˈpriːmiəm ˈprɒdʌkt/ n. 高端产品
vocabulary.example: The store sells a range of premium products at a higher price point.
vocabulary.translation: 这家商店出售一系列高端产品，定价相对较高。

vocabulary.entry: value version /ˈvæljuː ˈvɜːʃn/ n. 平价版本
vocabulary.example: The value version of the software offers basic features at a lower cost.
vocabulary.translation: 这款软件的平价版本以更低价格提供基础功能。

vocabulary.entry: brand habit /brænd ˈhæbɪt/ n. 品牌习惯
vocabulary.example: Brand habit often leads consumers to buy the same product repeatedly.
vocabulary.translation: 品牌习惯往往会让消费者反复购买同一款产品。

vocabulary.entry: be down to /bi daʊn tuː/ 归因于；取决于
vocabulary.example: The team's success is down to hard work and teamwork.
vocabulary.translation: 这支队伍的成功归因于努力拼搏和团队协作。

sentences.english: You might have heard the term 'brand loyalty'.
sentences.chinese: 你可能听过“品牌忠诚度”这个说法。

sentences.english: As we enter a 5th generation of console releases, with Sony's PS5 and Microsoft's Xbox series X due to hit our shelves this year, once more psychologists are predicting a wave of purchases based on fidelity.
sentences.chinese: 随着我们进入第五代游戏机的发售期，索尼的PS5和微软的Xbox Series X今年即将上架销售，心理学家再次预测，一波基于品牌忠诚度的购买热潮即将到来。

sentences.english: But why do people feel compelled to stick with brands?
sentences.chinese: 但为什么人们会忍不住忠于某个品牌呢？

sentences.english: Writer Carol M. Bopp describes brand loyalty as a positive feeling that consumers identify with a certain product or company.
sentences.chinese: 作家卡罗尔·M·博普将品牌忠诚度定义为消费者对某一产品或公司产生的认同感和好感。

sentences.english: This also draws on the idea of brand awareness: the extent to which customers are familiar with the logo or values of a brand, goods or a service.
sentences.chinese: 同时也借鉴了品牌认知度这一概念，也就是消费者对某个品牌、商品或服务的标志及价值观的熟悉程度。

sentences.english: Huge companies pump millions into marketing and advertising, using analytics to determine who is their ICP, or ideal customer profile.
sentences.chinese: 大型企业会投入数百万资金用于市场营销和广告宣传，并借助数据分析来确定自己的理想客户画像。

sentences.english: It’s no surprise that the ads which pop up on social media somehow feel targeted at or tailored for you.
sentences.chinese: 社交媒体上弹出的广告总能给人一种精准定位、为你量身定制的感觉，这一点也不奇怪。

sentences.english: This is because companies spend a lot of time and money analysing who is most likely to become loyal customers.
sentences.chinese: 因为企业会花费大量时间和资金，分析哪些人群最有可能成为其忠实客户。
这种现象也延伸到了超市领域。

sentences.english: Many believe that the more expensive branded products are much better than the supermarkets’ own brand.
sentences.chinese: 很多人认为，价格更贵的品牌商品比超市自有品牌的产品要好得多。

sentences.english: Money-saving experts like Martin Lewis, encourage us to give up the premium or branded products and buy the value versions.
sentences.chinese: 但马丁·刘易斯等省钱专家建议我们，放弃那些高端品牌商品，转而购买平价替代款。

sentences.english: So, are we really brand loyal?
sentences.chinese: 那么，我们真的是在忠于品牌吗？

sentences.english: Companies certainly want us to be.
But there are those who believe it's more to do with brand habit – that feeling of comfort you get from buying the same product over and over again.
sentences.chinese: 但有些人认为，这更多是一种品牌习惯——也就是反复购买同一款产品带来的舒适感。

sentences.english: Once we’re familiar with a brand and we know that it's OK, we don't feel compelled to try anything else.
sentences.chinese: 一旦我们熟悉了某个品牌，并且觉得它还不错，就不会再想去尝试其他品牌了。

sentences.english: So, the next time you find yourself buying your favourite brand, it might not be down to brand loyalty, but rather to habit, or even that you have been targeted by a specific company through tailored ads.
sentences.chinese: 所以下次当你又在购买自己喜欢的品牌商品时，这可能并非源于品牌忠诚度，而是出于习惯，甚至可能是因为你已经成为某家公司的精准营销目标。
